A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Bitween and retain the same core RSR-learning framework. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial changes in scope and organization.

before.justification: V1 reports original RSR-Bench and NLA-DigBench experiments, discovered properties, runtime and sample measurements, and regression comparisons.

after.justification: V2 reports original experiments across 80 benchmark functions, including symbolic and LLM comparisons, discovered properties, verification outcomes, runtimes and token usage.

M1.justification: V2 introduces Agentic Bitween: LLMs propose new query functions and iteratively invoke Bitween's inference and verification tools (Section 5 and Appendix F). This substantially extends the discovery procedure. The vanilla regression method persists; rational approximation added to its pseudocode was already described in v1.

E1.justification: RSR-Bench expands from 40 programs to 80 functions, adding inverse trigonometric functions, ReLU/GELU, discontinuous functions and special functions such as gamma and Gudermannian. Conversely, v1's 34-program NLA-DigBench invariant-inference evaluation and its separate interpolation/extrapolation scenario are removed.

E2.justification: V2 adds Deep Research comparisons using GPT-OSS-120B, Claude-Sonnet-4 and Claude-Opus-4.1 without Bitween tools. It removes DIG/SymInfer and polynomial interpolation, spline, MLP and KAN comparisons. MILP, PySR and GPLearn remain; the latter two were already evaluated qualitatively in v1's discussion.

E3.justification: V2 introduces matched LLM comparisons with and without Bitween tools, RSR counts distinguished from automatically verified identities, function coverage, verification rates and token measurements. It explicitly omits Gröbner reduction, whereas v1 reports reductions before selecting properties. The stated hardware, sampling interval, error bound and degree settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds analyses of tool access, model-dependent discovery, verification/inference calls and token-versus-runtime costs (Figures 2–4). V1's degree and extrapolation analysis for x sin(x), along with its cubes, Bresenham and square-root invariant case studies, is removed.

E5.justification: Both versions state that experiments were repeated five times. Neither provides seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or an identifiable significance test. V2's additional result rows do not introduce a different uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: V2 replaces and substantially expands the reported outcomes through Tables 2–6, while removing invariant and interpolation results. Its symbolic-method tables report 76 RSRs for LR, 54 for PySR, 47 for GPLearn and 64 for MILP, alongside extensive new agent results. These counts are not directly comparable with v1's 193 inferred properties under its earlier evaluation.

T1.justification: The central RSR definitions, Claims 6–7 and their proofs are retained, with the PAC comparison moved into appendices. V2 omits v1's separate epsilon-correctness definition and detailed per-regressor/refinement complexity expressions, constituting a limited removal of formal material.

C1.justification: V1 presents automated randomized reductions and invariant inference for mixed integer/floating-point programs as joint contributions. V2 centers mathematical RSR discovery, superiority over symbolic methods and LLM-driven discovery beyond fixed queries. The invariant-generation contribution and associated superiority claims disappear from the abstract, introduction and conclusion.

C2.justification: V2 attributes discovery gains to dynamic queries and tool-assisted verification, and argues that these gains justify higher computational costs. It adds limitations concerning redundant properties, incomplete discovery and token overhead. V1's detailed interpretations of MILP instability, invariant-tool failures and extrapolation behavior are removed.

D1.justification: Appendix F adds agent system prompts, exploration instructions and inference/verification tool interfaces. Conversely, v1's explicit 80/20 split, regression hyperparameter grids, MILP bounds and retry settings, C instrumentation instructions and web-interface access instructions are omitted. These omissions change reproducibility documentation without establishing that the underlying settings changed.

R1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix D substantially reposition the work around symbolic regression, automated mathematical discovery, neural-symbolic learning, LLM reasoning and active learning. New discussions include AI Feynman, DreamCoder and AlphaGeometry, while much of v1's invariant-generation and abstract-interpretation survey is removed.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution narrative, evaluation and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Related work moves earlier, part of the theory and the vanilla walkthrough move to appendices, and the standalone discussion and invariant-learning sections disappear. The title and variant terminology also change.

P2.justification: V2 introduces performance heatmaps, a radar chart, tool/token visualizations and a query-example table, plus substantially redesigned result tables and a long property catalogue. V1's invariant graphics, interpolation plots and timing/sample scatterplots are removed. The sigmoid figure is retained, and the overview moves from Figure 2 to appendix Figure 5.

improvement.justification: V2 adds a substantial agentic extension, broader evaluation, useful tool-access comparisons and explicit prompts. However, it removes detailed vanilla reproducibility information and reports potentially redundant property totals. Its evidence also contains unresolved errors: Tables 2–3 show LR coverage of 43/80 functions, versus 27% in Section 6, and Table 1's second sigmoid identity fails at x=y=1. These benefits and weaknesses prevent a reliable judgment of net overall quality improvement.
